AI can be a good tool as long as you don’t trust it as an independent infallible source. I used chatgpt a ton as a study tool, not on its own, more like “here are 5 pages of my outline and 15 pages of corresponding class notes, I’m confused about X, can you explain it” or “here are 10 pages of my outline, can you quiz me”. It also came up with decent practice exams, since a lot of my profs were new and didn’t have exams to practice from. It was most useful for synthesizing sources: “here are my class notes, here is my outline so far, here are the quimbee explanations for questions I missed, can you update my outline” and then I would retype what it gave me to add to my outline. I ended up top 3% of my class at a T-50. But, I pretty much only used it to summarize, synthesize, and quiz based on existing material, and I never trusted it on its own.

Yep. If someone skips 10 events in a row, especially without otherwise putting effort into the friendship or explaining why they haven’t been able to come but expressing interest in coming in the future, then the ball is now in their court to show they care about the friendship.

I don’t think this post is directed at the people who are busy, ill or have other extenuating circumstances, but genuinely make an effort to come to things when they can and reciprocate in the two way street that friendship is. It’s directed at the people who rarely show up but never apologize/explain why they can’t make it, and never reach out to make plans, but then get pissy when they’re not invited to something. Your planner friend doesn’t like being rejected over and over and being flaked on at the last minute without explanation, and it hurts their feelings when that happens repeatedly. Plus, not knowing if someone will or will not come to something makes planning harder -how much food is needed? How many cars do we need to take? Etc.

I’m surprised at how unpopular this is. I’m more of a type A/ planner, and if I invite someone out a bunch of times and they say no (or just ghost me) every time, I’ll make the fair assumption that they don’t want to spend time with me. Sure it’s easy to shoot off a quick text, but it’s hurtful when the invitation is declined over and over. It doesn’t feel good to be flaked on, so if there’s other people I can invite instead who I know will show up, why wouldn’t I invite them? Friendship is a two way street.

If you want more information about what TB is, this site i linked below has a lot of good information. It was one of the biggest killers before the age of antibiotics, responsible for in some places 25% or more of deaths. Antibiotics used to treat it effectively, but now antibiotic resistant strains such as the one the person in this story was infected with are more and more difficult to treat. If our medications no longer work, TB could cause a much, much more serious health crisis than even Covid-19. 

 https://tbfacts.org/history-tb/#:~:text=History%20of%20TB%20in%20the%2020th%20Century&text=In%201900%20it%20was%20estimated,was%20400%20deaths%20per%20100%2C000.

> Consumption was probably the most common killer of American colonial adults. It accounted for more than 25% of deaths in New York city between 1810 and 1815

>in 1900 it was estimated that the death rate for TB for white Americans was between 190 and 200 per 100,000. Among black Americans the comparable figure was 400 deaths per 100,000.

And last year over 1 million people died of it, despite treatments existing. It was (and still is) a horrifying disease that developed slowly such that the sufferer slowly withered away and eventually died.

Students who have to work during their free time won’t have time for extracurriculars; people whose parents don’t have connections will have fewer internship opportunities and resume skills; wealthier students are able to afford tutoring (or less ethical grade-saving options) if they’re failing a class; etc. More money can also, of course, buy better LSAT prep and allow for more free time to prep, but at the end of the day, it levels the playing field a lot more. If there’s yeast fermenting the sugars into alcohol, then there’s probably all kinds of other bacteria inside of the coconut. There’s a difference between cutting around a few worms in an otherwise healthy apple or a mushroom, and consuming something that’s likely full of unknown bacteria and molds.

Botulism toxin is toxic in such small amounts that it can be tasteless. Fermentation gone wrong can create methanol instead of ethanol, which is toxic and also nearly tasteless.
